title: arXiv AI papers — latest available batch: 2 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred, and citation evidence is sparse for such recent papers, so treat this as a relevance-led shortlist rather than a popularity ranking.

sections.title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
sections.abstract: MoSE3 predicts per-pixel 6-DoF motion from monocular video using 3D point tracks and rigidity embeddings, with a new synthetic articulated-motion dataset.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a feed-forward model for dense world-space SE(3) motion from monocular RGB plus Art-Kubric, reporting leading rigid/articulated motion and point-tracking benchmark results.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report sensitivity to upstream π³ camera geometry and track quality, especially under fast motion; deformable scenes are evaluated only qualitatively.

sections.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
sections.abstract: VERSE lets an LLM optimizer test and revise both an executor agent’s harness and its own tools and workflow, using execution checks to catch regressions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improvements on held-out SWE-rebench tasks and newer out-of-distribution tasks in five programming languages when VERSE is added to four evaluated harness optimizers.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says self-evolution’s incremental benefit varies by optimizer host; evaluation uses four reimplemented optimizers and benchmark task pools.

sections.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
sections.abstract: 4DCodeBench tests whether multimodal coding agents can turn videos into executable 3D scenes whose geometry and dynamics reproduce observed motion.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a 200-scene benchmark and report that static appearance and geometry reconstruction do not reliably transfer to complex dynamics.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that prescribed trajectories can score well without demonstrating learned physics; simulation’s generalization benefit remains untested.

sections.title: Lost in the Request: How Communication Variation Disrupts Retrieval and Action in Email Agents
sections.abstract: The authors vary request style and English dialect while holding task intent fixed, finding that indirect and formal phrasing can reduce email-agent task completion.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that verbosity can hinder lexical retrieval, while indirect and dialect variants can still harm performance after relevant evidence is retrieved.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is bounded to three evaluated systems and the paper’s five communication-style axes and four rule-based dialect conditions.

sections.title: LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients
sections.abstract: LESSER approximates gradient-based training-data selection from output-layer gradients, avoiding per-example backward passes while retaining batch-level alignment with full-gradient selection.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper presents output-layer gradients as a cheaper feature for data-selection methods and reports lower feature-extraction FLOPs on SFT and RL benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that output-layer and full gradients can rank individual examples differently; reported alignment is at the selected-batch level and results are bounded to evaluated benchmarks.

sections.title: CuBEs: Culturally-Situated Behavioral Evaluations and the Limitations of Culture-Blind LLM Judges
sections.abstract: CuBEs evaluates LLM behaviors in culturally situated scenarios and reports that judgments and behavior patterns vary across 12 cultures, including differences missed by culture-blind tests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose culturally situated behavioral evaluations and report that non-Western contexts can surface bias dimensions not captured by their culture-blind baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported scope is the paper’s 12 cultures, tested behavior scenarios, and 13 models; broader coverage is not established by the abstract.
